excluded.drop: never written in a Form: an owned value that nothing uses is dropped where its region ends, and the schedule writes the core's drop for it
excluded.io.byte: writes standard output outside λ; it stays in rce-core/1 for printed carriers only
excluded.mem.get: reads a memory array outside every value; it stays in rce-core/1 for printed carriers only
excluded.mem.set: writes a memory array outside every value; it stays in rce-core/1 for printed carriers only

status: proposal, not normative: written by hand and checked by spec/checker/tests/form_catalogue.rs until a chapter of the book defines rce-form/1, when rce-spec-data generates this file from it

terms.cell: true for the entries whose node names a memo cell of ω, ["memo",REF] or ["buffer",REF] (§10)
terms.clause: the sections of the RCE specification that define the operation; a rule label (N2, F1) follows its section
terms.domain: null for a total entry; for a partial entry, the domain fact of §7 that covers it and the tests that establish it on the same values as its operands. A test is an entry id, which means that entry gives false at the same type arguments on the same operands, or one of the named tests
terms.effect: the least effect class (§6: 0 total, 1 may halt, 2 emits, 3 host) of a function that holds the entry: 0 for an entry without ω, at least 1 for one with ω, since a function of class 0 holds no ω, and 2 for emit; no entry has class 3, since capabilities are cap nodes, not entries

exactness.exact-context: the parts of ω (the outputs λ, the fuel, the cost counters and the memo cells), changed exactly as the clause states
exactness.exact-integer: integers and truth values, computed exactly
exactness.exact-structure: arrays, lists, tuples and sums: values moved, copied or rearranged unchanged
exactness.ieee754: IEEE 754 binary64, or binary32 held as binary64: correctly rounded with roundTiesToEven where the operation rounds (F1 and the f32 rule of 6.3 N3), exact where it does not (F8), and never a value that is not finite (F4)

facts.DF1: the operand types imply the domain, a non-negative index or length included; it may stand for any test below whose name ends in not-negative
facts.DF3: guarded by a test of the divisor against 0 and by int.bad.quo
facts.DF4: inside the arm k of a Branch on sum.tag of the same value
facts.DF5: a non-negative index guarded by a test that it lies below the length of the same value
facts.DF6: a non-negative start, not after the end, and an end not after the length of the same value
facts.DF7: guarded by a test that the length of the same value is above 0
facts.DF8: a length that is not negative

terms.meaning: the operation's result in words; the clause and, until the vectors exist, one/eval.rs on the branch define it exactly

modes.consume: the operand is used up; a plain operand (bool, an integer, a float, bytes) may still be used elsewhere, since plain values may be used any number of times
modes.order: the order value ω, which comes back as the last result
modes.read-return: the operand comes back unchanged as the result whose of names it: the same value (§7)
modes.update-return: the operand comes back changed as the result whose of names it

terms.operands: the inputs of an Apply node of the entry, in order; a, b and c name operands 0, 1 and 2, and τ names type argument 0
terms.other_modes: selector, capture, carried and bound are the modes of the inputs of Branch and Iterate nodes (§8), never of an entry

params.body: any body type (§3) in which ["order"] does not occur
params.int-bitwise: an integer type of range [0, 2^k − 1] or [−2^(k−1), 2^(k−1) − 1], 1 ≤ k ≤ 64
params.int-zero: an integer type whose range holds 0
params.sum: a sum type ["sum",τ…] with at least one variant

patterns.index: ["index",i]: an integer literal k, the output of a Bind node, with 0 ≤ k below the number of components or variants of type argument i
patterns.int: ["int",lo,hi]: that integer type; an operand of ["int","-9223372036854775808","18446744073709551615"] takes any integer type, by integer-range inclusion (FG5)
patterns.other: ["bool"], ["f64"], ["f32"], ["bytes"], ["order"], and ["arr",P], ["list",P], ["tup",P…], ["sum",P…] over patterns P, as in §10
patterns.part: ["part",i,k]: the component or variant of type argument i whose number is the literal at operand k
patterns.parts: ["parts",i]: the component types of tuple type argument i, one operand or result per component, in order
patterns.repr: ["repr",i]: the body type that represents frame type argument i (§3)
patterns.tag: ["tag",i]: ["int","0",n − 1], n the number of variants of sum type argument i
patterns.within: ["within",P]: an integer type whose range lies inside P's; it stands inside another type, where the inclusion of FG5 does not reach

terms.results: the outputs, in order; of is the operand a result returns (read-return, update-return or order) and null for a new value; ω is always the last result
terms.symmetric: the two operand positions that may be exchanged without changing the results, which canonical rule C3 orders; empty when none

tests.divisor-not-zero: int.eq of operand 1 and 0 gives false
tests.end-not-after-length: int.le of operand 2 and the length of operand 0 gives true
tests.index-below-length: int.lt of operand 1 and the length of operand 0 (bytes.len, arr.len or list.len) gives true
tests.index-not-negative: operand 1 is not below 0, by its type (DF1) or by a test
tests.length-above-zero: the length of operand 0 is above 0
tests.length-not-negative: operand 0 is not below 0, by its type (DF1) or by a test
tests.start-not-after-end: int.le of operand 1 and operand 2 gives true
tests.start-not-negative: operand 1 is not below 0, by its type (DF1) or by a test
tests.tag-equals-index: the node lies in arm k of a Branch on sum.tag of operand 0, k being the literal at operand 1

terms.traps: the trap texts with which the entry may halt; partial entries never halt, since FG8 places each inside its domain

vectors: not part of this file: an entry's vectors (lang/vectors/catalogue/<entry>.json, rce-row-vectors/1) are checked on the Form evaluator (spec/checker/src/form/eval.rs, rce-form.md §2), which does not exist yet; until they are, no entry has joined a catalogue version and no catalogue key is fixed
